iut_type: End Product (JUST.WILL Bluetooth device using Espressif ESP32-S3 series module), module variant identification and RF/RF PHY test exemption
customer_question: We're developing a Bluetooth device using the ESP32-S3 -- after SIG registration, will certification testing be required, and roughly how much would it cost?
question_variants: Does it matter which specific ESP32-S3 module variant (antenna-integrated vs. antenna-connector) is used for test exemption purposes?
Does using an already radio-law-certified module variant exempt the product from its own radio-law procedure too?
actual_issue: The customer referred to 'ESP32-S3' generically without specifying which exact module variant within that series they intended to use, which mattered significantly for determining whether RF/RF PHY testing would be required and whether Japan's radio-law (construction-design) certification was already covered.
plain_english_explanation: ESP32-S3 is a series name covering multiple distinct module variants, not a single module -- the customer needed to specify exactly which variant they intended to implement. Two specific variants, the antenna-integrated ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 and the antenna-connector ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U, are both already qualified with Bluetooth SIG, meaning products implementing either of these exempts the product from RF/RF PHY testing for Bluetooth SIG registration purposes. Additionally, the WROOM-1U variant specifically has already obtained Japan's radio-law construction-design certification -- meaning a product implementing it does not need to separately obtain its own construction-design certification, as long as the module's existing certification number is displayed on the product.
consultant_answer: ESP32-S3 is a series name, not a single module -- could you confirm exactly which specific variant you're implementing? Two variants in particular, the antenna-integrated ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 and the antenna-connector ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U, are already qualified with Bluetooth SIG, so a product using either one is exempt from RF/RF PHY testing. The WROOM-1U variant has also already obtained Japan's radio-law construction-design certification, so your product doesn't need its own separate certification for that either -- you'd just need to display the module's existing certification number on your product.
decision_logic: When a customer references a module series name rather than a specific module variant/model number, confirm the exact variant before answering test-exemption or radio-law-certification questions, since different variants within the same series (e.g., antenna-integrated vs. antenna-connector) can have materially different exemption status for both Bluetooth SIG testing and national radio-law certification.
final_recommendation: When a customer references a module by series name only, proactively ask for the exact model number/variant before providing test-exemption guidance, and check both Bluetooth SIG qualification status and national radio-law certification status separately, since they are independent and a variant may be exempt from one but not the other.
risk_if_done_wrong: Answering test-exemption questions based on an assumed module variant, without confirming the customer's exact intended model, could lead to an incorrect cost/timeline expectation if the customer's actual chosen variant turns out not to be exempt.
